dishes.name: Rillettes de Tours
dishes.desc: Pork slowly cooked and shredded into a soft, golden spread, eaten on bread. Protected as a geographical indication and tied to the charcutiers of Touraine.

dishes.name: Rillons de Touraine
dishes.desc: Chunks of pork belly cooked gently until caramelised, eaten warm or cold, alone or with lentils and potatoes. A classic pairing with rillettes on Touraine charcuterie boards.

dishes.name: Sainte-Maure de Touraine
dishes.desc: The region's best-known goat cheese, a log with a straw running through its centre. It holds a protected designation and is sold in markets across the Tours area.

dishes.name: Nougat de Tours
dishes.desc: Not a nougat in the Provençal sense but a pastry: shortcrust topped with fruit compote, candied fruit and almonds. A traditional Tours sweet.

dishes.name: Beuchelle tourangelle
dishes.desc: A rich Touraine dish of sweetbreads and kidneys in a creamy mushroom sauce. Offal cooking in the old Tours style, found on traditional menus.
